hero.body: Resomix Catalogue Intelligence lets labels, publishers, distributors and libraries search a music catalogue by sound. Resomix's PYXIS-1 engine creates a sonic profile for every authorised recording and makes the catalogue searchable by sound. Start with one recording and discover ranked matches from across your catalogue.
hero.status: Guided partner evaluation · Authorised audio · Partner-scoped index
hero.captionA: ONE REFERENCE → PYXIS-1 → PARTNER CATALOGUE → RANKED MATCHES

hero.title: Make your catalogue [[discoverable by sound.]]

product.h2: One processed catalogue. Two outputs you can use.
product.body: Catalogue Intelligence is the catalogue-scale application of PYXIS-1. Once authorised recordings have been processed, each track can participate in discovery in two ways: as a reference that starts a search and as a candidate that can be returned when its sonic relationship is strong.
product.outABody: Submit a track or an audio reference and find the closest matches within your catalogue, carefully prioritised by PYXIS-1 similarity engine.
product.outBBody: When you need a closer look, open the full analysis of a recording: rhythm, harmony, timbre, structure, spectral character and energy.
product.note: Similarity retrieves related recordings. Track Intelligence explains one. Connected capabilities, not the same screen.
product.tiPreviewAria: Compact Track Intelligence preview: structure, energy, tempo, harmonic and timbre fields with fictional demonstration values.

flow.h2: Start with one track, and receive relevant recordings in your catalogue.
flow.body1: Use any track from your catalogue as a reference, or upload a new recording; PYXIS-1 compares it with your catalogue and returns the closest matches, ranked by similarity.
flow.body2: There's no need to build a result list manually or analyse your catalogue again with every search.
flow.figureAriaD: Two input routes, an indexed catalogue track using its existing profile or an authorised reference upload profiled before comparison, converge into one reference profile, are compared with the partner index, and return automatically ranked results.
flow.figureAriaM: Mobile flow: the two input routes converge into one reference profile, compared with the partner index, returning automatically ranked results.

trackIntel.h2: Open Track Intelligence when you want the full picture of a recording.
trackIntel.body1: Similarity tells you what sounds like your reference, while track Intelligence shows you what PYXIS-1 detects in a recording, from structure, harmony and rhythm to timbre, spectral characteristics and energy.
trackIntel.body2: Track Intelligence is a separate analysis view, available when you want to dig deeper into a recording. You don't need to analyse a track before receiving similarity matches.
trackIntel.figureAriaD: A wide Track Intelligence inspection panel for one fictional recording: structural waveform with labelled sections, energy journey, tempo and harmonic fields, and a restrained timbre view.
trackIntel.figureAriaM: Mobile Track Intelligence preview with structure, energy, tempo, harmonic and timbre fields.

value.h2: Give your deep catalogue another route into discovery.
value.body1: Metadata, release schedules and editorial priorities remain essential. PYXIS-1 adds another way to discover music: through the relationships within the audio itself. An older, niche, new or unreleased track can be recommended because it sounds right for the reference, and not because it already has a history of attention. why metadata alone isn't enough
value.body2: Resomix does not predict demand, guarantee exposure or decide what gets promoted. It simply makes more of the authorised catalogue findable when it is relevant to the sound being searched.
value.mod1Body: Older recordings can surface next to new releases when PYXIS-1 ranks them close in sound. how a back catalogue becomes reliable revenue
value.mod2Body: New or unreleased audio can be profiled and matched without waiting for streams, sales or interaction history.
value.mod3Body: One known recording can lead listeners or your team into parts of the catalogue that metadata alone would never surface. discovery as a revenue stream
value.figureAriaD: A horizontal release timeline: a recent active reference, an older quieter catalogue recording and three neutral candidates. One orange sonic relationship connects the reference to the older recording, which then appears in the ranked result list.
value.figureAriaM: Mobile: the recent active reference and the older catalogue recording connected by one sonic relationship; the older recording appears in the ranked results.

partner.h2: Add sonic retrieval without replacing the systems you already run.
partner.body1: Resomix sits alongside your existing tools as a discovery and analysis layer. In a guided pilot, you test catalogue similarity and Track Intelligence on an agreed sample. In a scoped integration, authorised server-side requests bring the results into your own product or workflow. Catalogues are delivered in batches through managed ingestion, and the private index is rebuilt as each batch lands.
partner.body2: You keep your catalogue, brand, licensing model and customer relationships. Resomix supplies the processing, sonic profiles and ranking behind them, as defined in the agreement.
partner.figureAriaD: Four-part architecture: the partner product or internal tool calls scoped API access, which reaches the partner sonic index and returns either ranked similarity results or a track analysis response.
partner.figureAriaM: Mobile integration: partner product, scoped API access, partner sonic index, then the two response branches.

boundary.h2: Your private catalogue does not become a shared partner pool.
boundary.body1: Authorised catalogue audio, derived profiles and the searchable index are restricted to the applicable partner scope. One partner’s private content is not exposed as another partner’s catalogue result. Access, retention and deletion follow the relevant written agreement.
boundary.body2: Partner catalogue processing starts only with authorised audio and metadata, supplied for the agreed service.
boundary.figureAriaD: Two completely separate bounded partner indexes served by the same PYXIS-1 capability with separate keys, separate queries and separate result lists. No line crosses between the two private catalogues.
boundary.figureAriaM: Mobile: the two partner indexes stacked and fully separate, each with its own key, query and results.

pilot.h2: Test PYXIS-1 on the music that matters to your team.
pilot.body: The right proof is not a generic accuracy claim. It is a controlled test on a representative sample of your own catalogue, using references your team knows and relevance criteria agreed up front.

s1.title: Scope the sample
s1.copy: Agree the catalogue sample, the use case, the authorised inputs and how results are judged.

s2.title: Deliver audio and metadata
s2.copy: Deliver the authorised recordings and agreed metadata through the managed partner workflow.

s3.title: Process and validate
s3.copy: PYXIS-1 creates the sonic profiles, the partner index is prepared and processing issues are reviewed.

s4.title: Run known-reference tests
s4.copy: Use references your team knows. Review the ranked results by listening and by product testing.

s5.title: Review the evidence
s5.copy: Weigh relevance, coverage, query speed and integration fit, then decide whether to expand.

items.q: How can a label make its back catalogue discoverable?
items.a: Resomix processes the authorised recordings once into a private, partner-scoped sonic index. From then on any track, old or new, can be returned when it sounds right for the reference, without waiting for streams, sales or editorial attention.

items.q: How do I find similar tracks inside our own catalogue?
items.a: Use any indexed track as the reference, or upload a recording. PYXIS-1 compares it with your catalogue and returns the closest matches, ranked by similarity, with no manual shortlisting.

items.q: Is our catalogue shared with other partners or made public?
items.a: No. Each partner's audio, derived profiles and index stay inside that partner's scope. There is no shared partner pool, and partner content is not made publicly available.

items.q: Is our audio used to train PYXIS-1?
items.a: No. Partner content is not used to train or fine-tune PYXIS-1, and Resomix does not generate derivative audio.

items.q: What do we need to deliver?
items.a: Authorised audio as MP3, WAV, FLAC or AIFF, and a CSV manifest with ISRC, title, artist and filename for each track, through the managed partner workflow.

items.q: How large a catalogue can Resomix process?
items.a: Catalogues are ingested in batches and the index is rebuilt as each batch lands, so the size is agreed per pilot rather than capped up front. A representative sample is enough to start.

closing.h2: Process the catalogue. Test the matches. Decide with evidence.
closing.body: Bring authorised audio, metadata and a few reference cases. Together we scope a guided pilot: catalogue similarity, Track Intelligence and integration fit. No full-catalogue commitment up front.
